newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot power prices fall with minimal demand.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot power prices fall with minimal demand.

text.p: Spot bulk power prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) dropped Monday with little demand due to mild temperatures in the state, industry sources said.
"There is hardly any load right now," said one ERCOT electricity seller.

Mild temperatures reaching highs in the 60s and low 70s degrees Fahrenheit were keeping power demand to a minimum, and many traders said they were not prescheduling electricity for Tuesday given the minimal interest.
ERCOT firm, peak power for a 16-hour block for Tuesday delivery was discussed at $18.00-21.00 from $25.00-29.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) late last week, the brokers and marketers said.
Firm off-peak ERCOT deliveries for Tuesday were notionally assessed at $8.00-10.00 from $15.00-19.00 on Friday for Monday business, the sources said.
Trading of non-firm peak and off peak power was said to be thin enough to be virtually non-existant.
February ERCOT peak power was thinly talked but was notionally reported to be holding steady at $30.00-31.75 per MWh.
